title: Ransomware Incident Response Protocol
steps: Detect and confirm: validate ransom notes, encryption activity and scope via EDR telemetry
Contain: isolate infected hosts and segments, disable remote access, block C2 indicators
Preserve evidence: capture memory and disk images before wiping
Assess: identify initial access vector, exfiltration and backup integrity
Eradicate: remove persistence, reset all privileged credentials, rebuild identity infrastructure if compromised
Recover: restore from clean immutable backups in business-priority order and monitor for reinfection
Notify: law enforcement, regulators and affected individuals per legal requirements
notes: Do not pay ransom without executive, legal and law-enforcement consultation. Sanctions screening is mandatory before any payment.

title: DDoS Mitigation Protocol
steps: Confirm attack via traffic baselines and distinguish from legitimate surge
Activate upstream ISP or cloud scrubbing and CDN protection
Apply rate limiting, geo-blocking and WAF rules to application endpoints
Fail over public communications to alternate channels (social media, radio, SMS)
Monitor for multi-vector or smokescreen attacks masking intrusion
Report to national CERT and capture traffic samples for attribution
notes: Public safety information channels require always-on DDoS protection.

title: Data Breach and Notification Protocol
steps: Stop ongoing exfiltration: disable vulnerable services and compromised accounts
Scope affected data types, records and jurisdictions
Engage forensics and preserve logs under legal privilege
Notify regulators within statutory deadlines (e.g. 72 hours under GDPR)
Notify affected individuals with clear guidance and support services
Remediate root cause and verify with independent testing
notes: Track regulatory clocks from the moment of awareness, not confirmation.

title: Industrial Control System (OT) Intrusion Protocol
steps: Prioritize physical safety: move affected processes to manual or safe state
Sever IT/OT connectivity and disable all remote access paths
Verify process values with independent field measurements
Increase quality and safety sampling of physical outputs
Engage OT-specialized incident response and notify sector regulator and CISA
Restore only after validating controller logic and firmware integrity
notes: Safety overrides cyber containment: never shut down safety instrumented systems.

title: Flood Emergency Response Protocol
steps: Monitor river gauges and forecasts; activate EOC at flood watch
Issue zone-based evacuation orders early and close low-water crossings
Protect critical facilities with temporary barriers and generators
Open shelters with accessible transport and pet accommodation
Conduct swift-water rescue with pre-staged boats and high-water vehicles
Issue public health advisories for water safety and contamination
Document damage for disaster declaration and recovery funding
notes: Most flood deaths occur in vehicles; road closure enforcement is life-saving.

title: Earthquake Response Protocol
steps: Activate EOC and conduct rapid windshield damage assessment
Deploy urban search and rescue to collapsed structures
Shut off gas in damaged zones and prioritize fire suppression
Establish casualty collection points and hospital surge coordination
Perform structural safety tagging of buildings, bridges and critical facilities
Restore communications with satellite and mobile cell assets
Open mass care shelters and family reunification services; prepare for aftershocks
notes: The first 72 hours are critical for live rescues.

title: Wildfire Evacuation Protocol
steps: Use pre-defined evacuation zones for warnings and orders
Notify residents via alerts, sirens and door-to-door in fast-moving fires
Manage evacuation traffic with contraflow and control points
Coordinate utility power shutoffs in high-risk circuits
Open evacuation centers with clean air spaces and animal care
Issue air quality advisories and distribute N95 masks
notes: Evacuate early; late evacuations in wind-driven fires cause entrapment.

title: Critical Infrastructure Outage Protocol (Power, Water, Telecom)
steps: Establish outage scope and estimated restoration time with the utility operator
Protect life-safety facilities first: hospitals, 911 centers, water and wastewater, dialysis
Deploy generators and fuel logistics for critical facilities
Open cooling or warming centers and conduct welfare checks on medically dependent residents
Issue public guidance: boil-water, carbon monoxide safety, alternate 911 numbers as applicable
Coordinate mutual aid crews and track restoration milestones publicly
notes: Maintain a registry of critical facilities and medically dependent residents.

title: Active Threat and Mass Casualty Protocol
steps: Neutralize the threat or stop the hazard (contact team, show-stop, halt crowd flow)
Deploy rescue task forces to treat casualties in warm zones
Establish unified command, staging, and casualty collection points
Perform START triage and distribute patients across hospitals
Secure the scene, preserve evidence and establish a family reunification center
Communicate through a single joint information center
notes: Stop the killing, stop the dying: time to hemorrhage control determines survival.

title: Hazardous Materials Release Protocol
steps: Identify the substance (placards, shipping papers, CHEMTREC) and consult ERG
Establish hot, warm and cold zones using plume modeling
Issue shelter-in-place downwind and evacuate high-risk zones
Deploy hazmat teams to control the release
Set up decontamination and alert hospitals of chemical exposures
Deploy air and water monitoring and publish results before re-entry
notes: Shelter-in-place is often safer than evacuation through a plume.

title: Public Health Outbreak Protocol
steps: Confirm cluster via case definitions and lab testing
Identify and remove the suspected source
Conduct epidemiological interviews and contact tracing
Notify affected populations with symptom and care guidance
Coordinate recalls with regulators and suppliers
Monitor for secondary cases until two incubation periods pass
notes: Early source removal is the most effective intervention.
